summary: A Pulse room message reads the contact's access once: NativePulseContact keeps that read for 60 s and every later packet of the same message (dialogue turn, handoff, Bridge submit, dispatch, T2 observation) reuses it instead of spawning the people owner again. Each packet still re-validates the kept value (state, rooms, owner, e164, expiry against the current clock). A failed read is never kept; a message that waits beyond 60 s (restart deferral) reads again.
reason: Amine 29/10: « pourquoi il faut checker à chaque message, on perd du temps et efficience ». On the S24 one allowlist read costs 2.1–2.8 s (python spawn); the paired write test showed 11 reads for one room message. Amine approved: one check per message.

tests.name: openclaw-plugin-mobile-ui/scripts/test-native-pulse-handoff.cjs
tests.evidence: 53/53: one read per message reused by its packets; a revoked contact is refused at the next message and, past 60 s, inside the same message; a failed read is not reused.

tests.name: openclaw-plugin-mobile-ui/scripts/test-native-pulse-paired.cjs
tests.evidence: 49/49 against playbooks 067fb028: a complete room write runs with 1 access read (11 before).

tests.name: openclaw-plugin-mobile-ui/scripts/test-native-fast-paired.cjs
tests.evidence: 23/23 against playbooks 0d267872: 7 reads for 6 messages (one stale refresh); a stale read is revalidated before the subprocess.

capabilities.reason: Same room actions and refusals; fewer owner spawns per message.

architecture.reason: The read is kept inside the existing per-message admission object; no cache, store or daemon is added.

limitations: The Python side still re-checks its sealed in-process evidence at each send (no spawn).
A revocation made during a message already in progress takes effect within 60 s or at the next message.
rollback: Revert this commit and redeploy the core.
